cards.design_implication: If implementing a similar code comparison study, define the simulation window as the first ~500 ms after core bounce and specify the initial stellar model as a spherically-symmetric 20 M ⊙ progenitor.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We compare the early (first ∼500 ms after core bounce) spherically-symmetric evolution of a 20 M ⊙ progenitor star from six different core-collapse supernovae codes: 3DnSNe-IDSA, AGILE-BOLTZTRAN, FLASH, F ornax , GR1D, and PROMETHEUS-VERTEX.
limitations: This claim is supported only by abstract-level text and does not provide details on specific code versions, initial condition file formats, or boundary condition implementations.
cards.statement: The study design involves comparing the early spherically-symmetric evolution of a 20 M ⊙ progenitor star using six different core-collapse supernova codes over the first ~500 ms after core bounce.

cards.design_implication: To replicate this comparison metric, ensure that shock radius evolution and total neutrino heating are calculated and recorded as primary quantitative outputs.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Given the diversity of neutrino transport and hydrodynamic methods employed, we find excellent agreement in many critical quantities, including the shock radius evolution and the amount of neutrino heating.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence lists these as 'critical quantities' but does not define the exact mathematical formulas, time-resolution, or numerical methods used to derive them.
cards.statement: Critical quantities measured for comparison in this abstract include shock radius evolution and the amount of neutrino heating.
